10735.author: Parsifal-2045
10735.body:
This PR implements a few new `nvcc` flags to speed-up device code compilation. In particular:
- [--split-compile number](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-compiler-driver-nvcc/index.html#split-compile-number-split-compile) to try and automatically divide heavy TUs into smaller chunks
- [--threads](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-compiler-driver-nvcc/index.html#threads-number-t) to allow parallel compilation of device-code TUs
- [--jobserver](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-compiler-driver-nvcc/index.html#jobserver-jobserver) to make it so both the split and the threads rely on the same jobs spawned by Make

I have performed some local measurements on a node equipped with 2 AMD EPYC 9534 using [#51085](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/51085) to pull about 25% of CMSSW and especially the `RecoTracker/PixelSeeding` package as one of the slowest to compile for device. I have also disabled rocm compilation to isolate the effects on the CUDA side. I attach here the results from time for each compilation step (starting from `scram b clean` before every pass):
```
Default compilation time:
real    13m16.469s
user    569m49.105s
sys     254m48.762s
Default RecoTracker/PixelSeeding compilation time:
real    9m39.174s
user    33m22.067s
sys     7m16.893s
New flags compilation time:
real    8m25.389s
user    510m24.473s
sys     107m21.013s
New flags RecoTracker/PixelSeeding compilation time:
real    2m32.060s
user    34m28.999s
sys     7m36.785s
```

Note: **Requires https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw-config/pull/120 to be able to correctly parse the `--jobserver` flag**

45216.author: felicepantaleo
45216.body:
### Description

This pull request introduces `vFloat` and `float` types in the `ParameterSets` of the CMSSW framework. The changes aim to improve the precision and performance of floating-point parameter handling in configuration sets.

A new Entry type code is added for float/vfloat. Files that store a float parameter in their configuration provenance cannot be read by releases that do not contain this change (FormatIncompatibility: Unknown ParameterSet Entry type encoding: 'H'). Encodings of existing double parameters are unchanged.

### Changes

1. Added `vFloat` and `float` type definitions.
2. Updated relevant configuration files to utilize the new types.
3. Ensured compatibility with existing functionality and modules.

This will allow the developers of C++ modules to directly use `std::vector<float>` configuration parameters avoiding manually converting each of them from  `std::vector<double>`, if double precision is not needed.


### Testing

- Ran all existing unit tests.
- Added new tests to cover the `vFloat` and `float` types.
- Tested with workflow `24900.0`.
- Verified no regressions in performance or functionality.

### Future Work

If the tests run smoothly, an existing reconstruction module will be migrated from `double` to `float` within this pull request.

@smuzaffar @makortel @Dr15Jones @fwyzard @rovere @VinInn FYI
45216.title: Introduce vFloat and float types in ParameterSets

51042.author: EmanueleCoradin
51042.body:
#### PR description:

This PR introduces a DNN-based High-Purity (HP) pixel track selection for Phase-2 HLT pixel tracking using the PyTorch Alpaka package.

This PR is coupled with #51085, which introduces some changes and updates to the Patatrack pixel tracking.

Main changes:

* Added `PixelTrackTorchHighPuritySelector`, an Alpaka EDProducer performing the selection.
* Updated HLT Phase-2 pixel tracking sequences to use the DNN HP selector output.
* Removed the Cut-Based selector from the Phase-2  pixel tracking sequence.

Expected impact:

* Enables vertex-independent HP pixel-track selection using DNN inference.
* Simplifies the Phase-2 HLT heterogeneous pixel tracking workflow by removing the circular dependency between vertexing and HP track selection.

Related material:

* [Presentation at tracking POG](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1680142/#92-update-on-pixel-track-dnn-a), with the combined effect of this PR and #51085.

## PR description:
Overhaul of the output folder structure for Tracker DQM. Moving towards a detector-structure-based DQM system as seen in Run3, rather than separating DQM histograms into different folders for each product.
Fixed some histograms that were not filling properly and removed some that were not helpful for DQM.
Output of DQM available [here](https://cernbox.cern.ch/files/link/public/5RxHnXE4JymEmQ9). Contains both a "master" and "restructure" file for comparison purposes - restructure also contains X/Y/Z/Phi plots for each shell in the Inner Tracker, which are not present in the final code/DQM output (they are only there to illustrate/confirm the shell shapes).
Updated README.

[Presentation](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1628660/sessions/660498/attachments/3260480/5821281/TkDQM_Ph2_ideas_Apr26.pdf) by @alaperto with motivations for changes
[Presentation](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1698995/contributions/7145383/attachments/3297982/5898670/DQM_folder_restructure.pdf) with a brief overview of changes

#### Folder changes:

- All DQM plugins previously using `TrackerPhase2OT<product>` or `TrackerPhase2TT<product>` as a top folder are changed to use `OuterTracker` (exception of TrackerPhase2OTL1Track)
- All DQM plugins previously using `TrackerPhase2IT<product>` as a top folder are changed to use `InnerTracker`
- Added shells and half-cylinders to the inner tracker folder structure **in DQM and Validation** (now split into mI/mO/pI/pO)
  - Added a helper function to get the shell name of a det
- Added wheels to inner tracker and outer tracker endcap folder structure **in DQM only** (now contains both `Ring_<x>` and `Wheel_<x>` folders)
  - Added a helper function to get folder path for wheels
  - In order to book and fill all DQM layer histograms in both Rings and Wheels, booking and filling is looped over twice in endcap modules with the Ring folder as the first book/fill and the Wheel folder as the second.
- Endcap side1/side2 changed to Endcap PLUS or Endcap MINUS
- Moved "Global Position" histograms into a dedicated `/Positions` folder
- Added "V" to Digi validation folders.

#### DQM Histogram Changes

- All_Histogram_Names_Now_Look_Like_This
- Any "numberof" or "n" or generally counting histograms renamed to "Num_"
- RecHit histograms have "Cluster" removed from their names, now only use "RecHit"
- All histograms now specify the product in the histogram name & title
- Expanded x range of Num_Hit_Detectors_Per_Layer 

#### Inner Tracker histogram changes

- Cluster_LocalPosition_XY removed: not useful
- RecHit_LocalPosition_XY removed: not useful
- Digi_LocalPosition_XY removed: not useful
- Fixed scale of Digi Global Position histograms
- Fixed typo in NumberOfClustersLayer

#### Outer Tracker histogram changes

- Cluster_LocalPosition_XY removed: not useful
- Num_Clusters_Barrel moved to /Barrel folder
- RecHit GlobalPosition_perlayer_XY removed: broken and not useful even if working
- RecHit LocalPosition_XY removed: not useful
- Num_RecHits fixed (previously did not fill)
- Num_RecHits_layer_P fixed (previously filled with both P and S data)
- Num_RecHits_layer_S added
- L1Clusters: folder migrated to detector-style structure
- L1Stub: folder migrated to detector-style structure
- Digi_LocalPosition_XY removed: not useful

51489.author: fdoljanin
51489.body:
# Improve DisplacedParticleGun

#### PR description:

This PR improves the sampling and configuration of `DisplacedParticleGunProducer`.

The particle origin is now sampled at z=0, using either a uniform-area or uniform-radius distribution. The trajectory is then required to cross the configured production region and, when present, an optional target region. Additional geometry checks and constrained direction sampling make failures from incompatible configurations much less likely.

The production-vertex time is calculated from the distance travelled from the origin and the particle velocity, fixing the previous timing offset.

The displaced-particle upgrade workflow now uses the `CloseBy` beam spot instead of `DBrealisticHLLHC`.

The configuration was reorganized to describe the momentum, origin, production region, and optional target region explicitly.

#### PR validation:

- Successfully compiled with `scram b`.
- Passed `scram build code-checks`.
- Passed `scram build code-formats`.
- Generated events with several different configurations without errors.
- Verified that workflow `34554.0` selects `GenSimDisplaced` with the `CloseBy` beam spot.

51542.author: brandiskip
51542.body:
This PR adds track-level rate monitoring (fake rate, duplicate rate, and per-event track rate) to the Phase2 Outer Tracker L1 track validation, for both the **nominal (prompt)** and **extended (prompt + displaced)** L1 track collections. All quantities are MC-truth based (`TTTrackAssociationMap` / `isGenuine`) and follow the definitions in [L1TrackNtuplePlot.C](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/L1Trigger/TrackFindingTracklet/test/L1TrackNtuplePlot.C).

### Analyzer: [Phase2OTValidateTracks.cc](https://github.com/brandiskip/cmssw/blob/l1tk-phase2-track-rate-fake-dup-monitoring/Validation/SiTrackerPhase2V/plugins/Phase2OTValidateTracks.cc)
- New `processTrackRates()` loops over the reconstructed L1 tracks and fills, per collection: `trk_all_vspt` (denominator), `trk_fake_vspt` (tracks failing `isGenuine`), and the per-event multiplicities `ntrk_pt2` / `ntrk_pt3` / `ntrk_pt10`.
- Duplicate counting added in `processTrackCollection()`: for each tracking particle, every genuine L1 track matched to it beyond the first fills `trk_duplicate_vspt`.
- New ingredient histograms booked under `Nominal_L1TF/TrackRateIngredients` and `Extended_L1TF/TrackRateIngredients`; `TH1Track_pt` and `TH1NTracks` PSets added to `fillDescriptions`.

### Harvester: [Phase2OTHarvestTracks.cc](https://github.com/brandiskip/cmssw/blob/l1tk-phase2-track-rate-fake-dup-monitoring/Validation/SiTrackerPhase2V/plugins/Phase2OTHarvestTracks.cc)
Forms the final rate plots under `Nominal_L1TF/FinalRates` and `Extended_L1TF/FinalRates`:
- `fakeFraction_vspt` = `trk_fake_vspt / trk_all_vspt` 
- `duplicateFraction_vspt` = `trk_duplicate_vspt / trk_all_vspt` 
- `trackRate_vspt` = `trk_all_vspt / nEvents` 

### Helpers: [TrackerPhase2HistUtil.h](https://github.com/brandiskip/cmssw/blob/l1tk-phase2-track-rate-fake-dup-monitoring/Validation/SiTrackerPhase2V/interface/TrackerPhase2HistUtil.h)
- Added `bookFraction()` (num/den via `TH1::Divide(..., "B")`) and `bookPerEventRate()` (counts / `nEvents` with `Sumw2`), removing duplicated harvesting code.

### DQM output
Users will see the new histograms under `TrackerPhase2OTL1TrackV`  `{Nominal_L1TF, Extended_L1TF}`  `{TrackRateIngredients, FinalRates}`.

Full set of histograms can be reviewed [here](https://cernbox.cern.ch/files/spaces/eos/user/b/bskipwor/public/ValidationPlots?items-per-page=100&files-spaces-generic-view-mode=resource-table&tiles-size=2) under `TrackerPhase2OTL1TrackV`.

### PR validation
```
scram build code-checks
scram build code-format
```
51542.title: Phase2OT L1 track validation: add fake/duplicate/track-rate plots

51550.body:
#### PR description:

Continuation of the TrackExtenderWithMTD refactoring started in [#51374](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/51374).

Moves hit-matching logic out of TrackExtenderWithMTD and into a new standalone MTDHitMatcher class (analogous to TrackTransformer), exported as a library from RecoMTD/TrackExtender.

MTDHitMatcher owns the MeasurementEstimator, the TransientTrackingRecHit builder, and all chi/bsTimeSpread configuration. It exposes:

matchBTL()  delegates to matchLayers() with allBTLLayers()
matchETL()  filters to same z-side, delegates to matchLayers(), sorts output innermost-first
matchLayers() (private)  the shared loop over find_hits_in_dets() and fillMatchingHits(); no logic duplication
The plugin config gains a nested "MTDHitMatcher" PSet (analogous to "TrackTransformer"), grouping: estimatorMaxChi2, estimatorMaxNSigma, btlChi2Cut, btlTimeChi2Cut, etlChi2Cut, etlTimeChi2Cut, bsTimeSpread, MTDRecHitBuilder.

TrackExtenderWithMTD::produce() now calls matcher_.matchBTL()/matchETL() with two lines each, making a planned intermediate BTL refit a one-line insertion between those two calls.

No logic changes.

PU200 RelMon (pr3 vs master+#51374, 827 MTD histograms, b2b KS t=0.99999): 827/827 passing (100%)

51562.author: felicepantaleo
51562.body:
Turns the pileup-aware MC-truth graph on for Run4, wired entirely under the `enableTruth` process modifier and added to the `Phase2C22I13M9` era (so `Phase2C26I13M9` and the `noMkFit` variants inherit it). No special workflow is needed.

The truth is built once, at the mixing/DIGI step, where the merged signal+pileup sim-hits are live: the `TruthGraphAccumulator` builds the merged raw graph during mixing, and the logical graph plus a per-particle per-cell hit index are built right after it. RECO consumes those products (the branch validators and association producers read them by `DetId`); it does not rebuild anything.

## Event-content levels

Two orthogonal choices. The first is the one that matters for cost; the second is an advanced
option for special downstream consumers.


### 1. Detector scope (the size/cost lever)

| Level | Channels captured + indexed | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **`default`: full detector** | Calo (HGCAL + ECAL barrel + HCAL), **Tracker**, **Muon**, **MTD** | Complete truth for **track-based** candidate matching: a `TICLCandidate` is two-channel (calo shared-energy plus tracker shared-hits), so full particle-flow / candidate-PID validation needs the tracker channel. |
| **`reduced`: calo + MTD + muon** | above **minus Tracker** | Cost-sensitive opt-out (`customiseTruthReduced`): drops the tracker, the largest sim-hit family, keeping the calorimeter + timing + muon truth a calo-only TICL study needs. |

The default is the **full detector**: it captures every channel a two-channel candidate metric needs.
`reduced` (`customiseTruthReduced`) drops only the tracker `PSimHit`s, which dominate the merged sim-hit volume, for a cheaper calo + MTD + muon truth. The calorimeter channel `HitChannel::Calo` holds all calorimetry (HGCAL endcap plus ECAL barrel and HCAL), keyed by DetId type.

### 2. Persistence of the per-cell footprint (advanced, orthogonal)

Every level persists the compact truth:

- `truthLogicalGraphProducer`, the navigable Particle-Vertex logical graph;
- `truthLogicalGraphHitIndexProducer`, the per-particle per-cell hit index, **unresolved** (`recHitMap=""`). It is keyed by `DetId`, which is what the shared-energy association matches on, so the same index serves L1, HLT and offline RECO; `recHitIndex` is resolved on demand per stage;
- `TruthGraph_mix`, the raw merged CSR graph (small; the branch validators consume it and it allows
  an offline rebuild).

An opt-in `+simHits` variant additionally keeps the merged sim-hits (`mix:merged*Hits`). It is the only variant that lets a consumer rebuild the association at a **different granularity** (e.g. L1 trigger cells) or with a different metric, at the cost of the raw sim-hit size. Not needed for standard calo/tracker shared-energy truth.

### Why the index is unresolved and DetId-keyed

The association layer (`BranchHitAssociator`) matches reco objects to truth branches by `DetId`, computing a hits-and-fractions shared energy with the **per-cell total sim energy as the denominator**. Because it is `DetId`-based, the DIGI-built index is stage-independent and the bulky merged sim-hits never have to cross the DIGI to RECO boundary in the default content. 

## Cost (measured)

A/B (truth off vs on), single-thread, rough and directional (2 to 3 events), not a production benchmark.

**GEN-SIM**: `g4SimHits.TrackingAction.ReconnectDroppedAncestors` is now a baseline default, on unconditionally (no longer gated by `enableTruth`). It is a general SimVertex-connectivity correctness fix, not truth-specific: it only fixes up `SimVertex::parentIndex` so nothing orphans.
Measured essentially free (TTbar: CPU ~0%, output size unchanged, peak RSS within noise). All the truth cost is at DIGI. Because every GEN-SIM now has this connectivity, no truth-specific MinBias pileup sample is needed.

**DIGI** (PU200, DIGI+L1 step), both content levels:

| Metric | `default` (full detector) | `reduced` (calo + MTD + muon) |
|---|---|---|
| Total CPU | **~+23%** | ~+8% |
| Peak RSS | +290 MB (+6%) | +247 MB (+5%) |
| DIGI-RAW size | **~+11.7 MB/ev (~17%)** | ~+9.5 MB/ev (~14%) |

(Muon is a ~1k hits/event family, so it does not move the calo + MTD numbers.)

DIGI-RAW breakdown for `reduced` (per event, compressed): hit index ~6.3 MB, raw graph ~2.8, logical
graph ~0.4. The tracker merge and its index channel are the bulk of the difference between the levels:
the default roughly triples the DIGI CPU delta versus reduced for about 2 MB/ev more output.

Per-module profiling: the truth build producers cost ~0.4 s/event (negligible). The entire cost is the accumulator's sim-hit merge inside the MixingModule. Sim-hit families merged per event at PU200 (full level, for reference): ECAL 1.9M, HGCal 0.56M, tracker 0.55M, MTD 0.12M, HCAL 40k, muon 1k.

It's excluded where it cannot work:

- **Premixing** (`premix_stage2`): premixed pileup carries no raw pileup `SimTrack`s, so the
  accumulator has nothing to build from. The accumulator and the build are dropped under premix.
- **FastSim**: no full-sim `g4SimHits`; the `fastSimPhase2` helper drops `enableTruth` from every FastSim era.
51562.title: Enable the MC-truth graph with configurable event-content levels

51563.author: felicepantaleo
51563.body:
Introduces TICLGeom, a portable (host and device) structure-of-arrays geometry for HGCAL, and migrates the HGCAL and TICL reconstruction, validation and associators off hgcal::RecHitTools onto it.

TICLGeom is built once per run by an EventSetup producer and holds, per cell (sorted by rawDetId):

  • the geometry quantities RecHitTools derives from CaloGeometry (position, radius, wafer and tile information), as plain columns in a PortableCollection (SoABlocks: common, silicon, scintillator);
  • a rawDetId to dense-index lookup, an arithmetic hash-free block table usable in Alpaka kernels via ticlgeom::denseIdOf;
  • per-layer positions (the getPositionLayer replacement).

A host and device facade ticlgeom::Tools mirrors the RecHitTools API, so the roughly 40 consumers read geometry from columns (or decode detid bits directly) instead of doing CaloGeometry map lookups. The same layout is usable on device, which is the enabler for moving CLUE3D and the TICL chain to kernels later.

Packages migrated: RecoHGCal/TICL, RecoLocalCalo/HGCalRecProducers and HGCalRecAlgos, Validation/HGCalValidation, SimCalorimetry/HGCalAssociatorProducers, RecoEgamma/EgammaTools, RecoParticleFlow/PFClusterProducer, and the HLT configuration.

EventSetup wiring

The producers are @alpaka EventSetup producers. In reco they attach only under phase2_hgcal, so they never leak into FastSim or Run 2/3 processes. At HLT they are provided by self-contained HLT cfi under the same EventSetup labels the offline reco uses (no import of the reco cff), with a barrel-inclusive (ECAL+HCAL+HGCal) instance attached under ticl_barrel for the barrel layer clustering and CLUE3D.

Physics validation

Physics-neutral. A/B on the same GEN-SIM (TTbar Run4D121 PU200): 38841 of 38842 HGCAL validation histograms are bit-identical between the release and this branch. The single difference is one TICLCandidate out of about 21000 crossing a PID-category boundary, with the category integral conserved, from storing positions as float rather than double. That is the expected float-truncation boundary effect and is within tolerance.

Timing

Matched A/B on the same TTbar Run4D121 PU200 events, one socket, single thread, FastTimerService time_real. A is the release (RecHitTools), B is this branch.

Per-module, per event, for the geometry-lookup-heavy consumers, measured independently at HLT and offline:

module | HLT | offline -- | -- | -- HGCalLayerClusterProducer | -17.5% | -15.7% TrackstersProducer (CLUE3D) | -11.3% | -10.9% HGCalRecHitProducer | -22.7% | -14.9% TICLLayerTileProducer | -23.2% | -8.5% affected modules, total | -11.7% | -10.1%

FilteredLayerClusters, TICLCandidate and TracksterLinks are unchanged within noise (they use detid bit-methods and cluster data, not per-cell geometry lookups). The two large modules agree to within 2 percent across the two independent processes.

Overall per event -3%

The SoA is built once per run in the EventSetup producer, which currently costs about 13 s at HLT because it fills every cell by calling RecHitTools. This is a one-time, per-run cost that amortizes over the run; reducing it is a follow-up.

Follow-ups (separate PRs)

  • A dedicated EventSetup record instead of CaloGeometryRecord, so TICLGeom can depend on conditions (dead cells, calibration, alignment) with a correct IOV.
  • Speeding up the one-time SoA build.
51563.title: TICLGeom: a portable SoA geometry

51571.author: slava77
51571.body:
The primary target is high-pt jet events. This should have an incremental improvement for #51245 

in the 17.0.0pre2 relval GEN-SIM c78d2621-e964-4ec4-baf0-31eb50b6e2bd.root LS:190 had some slow events (4th:5404 7th:5407); a large fraction of time was in the `ExtendT5FromDupT5` kernel. This is partly covered in the discussion thread of #51245 

Two updates were made:
- For the case with `kT5DuplicateMinSharedHits == 8` there is a possible shortcut in the logic where a large fraction of modules or T5s can be skipped early.
- the thread use for cases with modules with many T5s is suboptimal (parallelizes only over modules; as a result only one thread per warp does any work in majority of cases). This part was refactored to collect compatible modules first and then parallelize the loop over T5s rather than the modules.

The updates are expected to be technical (no change in the physics results). The timing/profiling was measured in CMSSW_17_0_0_pre2 after the commits from #51333 (the last relevant change from 20X)

CPU side (using igprof; reference -> 1st change -> 2nd change):
- 10 events from the slow relval 2TeV job (per event): 56.6 s -> 7.0 s -> 6.9 s
- ttbar PU200 benchmark (per event, over 100 evts): 7.70 ms -> 6.60 ms -> 7.2 ms

GPU side is less impressive (times via nsys; reference -> 1st change -> 2nd change):
- 10 events from the slow relval 2TeV job (per event): 3.83 s -> 2.45 s -> 0.228 s
    - the slowest event: 33.8 s -> 21.6 s -> 2.12 s
- ttbar PU200 benchmark (per event, over 100 evts): 0.179 ms -> 0.198 ms -> 0.130 ms

Overall, about a factor of 10 speedup in `ExtendT5FromDupT5` kernel for the high-pt jets (2 TeV events) and some minor speedup in ttbar (this kernel itself was taking about 1/4 of the total LST processing time on CPU)
51571.title: LST: speedup ExtendT5FromDupT5 kernel

51575.author: Parsifal-2045
51575.body:
#### PR description:

With the introduction of the new `cudaKernelStackBudget` tool in #51395, it was noted that the largest kernel spill in a typical Phase-2 configuration was due to the `find_ntuplets` kernel of the PixelTracking CA. This PR proposes a fix to significantly reduce the spill.
The kernel is templated on a `maxDepth` parameter (currently 12), which leads to the creation (and allocation in thread-local memory) of multiple copies of the kernel-local `hits` array after template unrolling. The fix instead passes the hits indexes array as a kernel argument removing the duplication entirely.

#### PR validation:

The code compiles and runs, producing identical result in a typical Phase-2 TTbar workflow (comparison plots [here](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/reduceCASpill/hltPhase2Pixel_hltAssociatorByHits/)).

Furthermore, the output of `cudaKernelStackBudget` changes significantly.
Before:
```
device 0: NVIDIA H100 NVL (compute capability 9.0, sm_90)
  max resident threads: 270336
  reservation (launched kernels): 301.1 MiB (315752448 B) = 270336 threads x 1168 B
      largest stack frame 1168 B in pluginRecoTrackerPixelSeedingPortableCudaAsync.so
      kernel: alpaka_cuda_async::caHitNtupletGeneratorKernels::Kernel_find_ntuplets<pixelTopology::Phase2OT>  [hltPhase2PixelTracksSoA]
      shared memory: 1024 B total = 1024 B static + 0 B dynamic
```
After:
```
device 0: NVIDIA H100 NVL (compute capability 9.0, sm_90)
  max resident threads: 270336
  reservation (launched kernels): 78.4 MiB (82182144 B) = 270336 threads x 304 B
      largest stack frame 304 B in pluginRecoLocalTrackerSiPixelClusterizerPluginsPortableCudaAsync.so
      kernel: alpaka_cuda_async::pixelClustering::FindClus<pixelTopology::Phase2>  [hltPhase2SiPixelClustersSoA]
      shared memory: 36752 B total = 36752 B static + 0 B dynamic
```
(`kernel_find_ntuplets` sits at 160 B STACK after)

The reduction in the largest stack frame is expect to show up as a meaningful reduction in the overall GPU memory usage during benchmarks (~220 MiB per job).
51575.title: Reduce GPU kernel spill due to the PixelTracking CA

51583.author: Parsifal-2045
51583.body:
#### PR description:

`HLTrigger/Configuration/python/HLT_HeterogeneousOnly_cff.py` and the `DST_HeterogeneousReco` path it schedules are maintained by hand: every new `@alpaka` module, and every change to what feeds one, has to be mirrored there and no concept of procModifiers is available in a menu.

This PR adds `hltDumpHeterogeneous`, which derives the same thing from a cmsDriver configuration, for example:
```
hltDumpHeterogeneous --manifest manifest.json -o het_dump.py -- gpu_config.py
```
Strips out all non-heterogeneous modules from `gpu_config.py` and produces a runnable dump of only the heterogeneous modules and their minimal dependency set, saved in `het_dump.py`. Starting from an already-made `cmsDriver` config, allows the dump to respect `procModifiers` and all other form of process customisation. The dependencies are extracted from the framework, through a zero-event run with the `Tracer` service: the input configuration therefore has to be runnable.

The heterogeneous modules, wrapped in `HLTBeginSequence` + `hltL1GTAcceptFilter` before and `HLTEndSequence` after, are collected in a path (default `DST_HeterogeneousReco`) with dependencies stored in a `Task` associated with the `Path`. Finally, the dump produces a `Schedule` with the `Paths` whose status is consumed, the new `Path`, then `HLTriggerFinalPath` and `HLTAnalyzerEndpath`.
The optional `--manifest` flag produces a JSON file that records what was kept, which dependency was pulled in by what, and which products are expected from the input file.

Nothing outside `HLTrigger/Configuration` is touched, and no existing configuration changes behaviour.

#### PR validation

Run on two Phase-2 recipes, both with `--procModifiers alpaka` to include all currently available heterogeneous modules:

- `-s L1P2GT,HLT:75e33_timing` reproduces the existing `DST_HeterogeneousReco` exactly.
- the same with `--procModifiers ngtScouting,alpaka` gives 18 modules, missing exactly the nine modules of the LST branch that menu does not schedule, including the legacy pixel-track chain that only fed LST.

The L1 emulation is counted separately in both cases (43 modules on 41 Paths and is pulled in as a dependency of the accept filter.

`testHeterogeneousClosure` adds 25 unit tests covering the `Tracer` parser, the closure and stop rules, path-status dependencies, the `Path`/`Task` split and the `EventSetup` pruning.
51583.title: Add `hltDumpTaggedModules` configuration dumper for heterogeneous-only configs
